title: End-to-end tests with Playwright and Cypress

videos.script:
So far the planner has run in a document that does not exist. {{jsdom}} Today it runs in Chromium, the browser Chrome is built from, with CSS, a network and a clock.

Playwright drives the browser from outside. {{pw}} Your test opens the page, clicks the link, fills in the form, and reads the total. The test stops the browser's clock on the twenty-first of October, so the week is the same every day.

Browsers do things on their own time. {{flaky}} So you meet a flaky test on purpose. It reads the page once, too early, and fails. The cure is to assert, and let Playwright retry.

When a test fails, Playwright records the page. {{trace}} You read the failure without opening anything.

Then Cypress, the other tool you will meet. {{cypress}} It runs inside the browser instead. The habits are the same.

Last, the bill. {{cost}} A browser test costs hundreds of times more than a unit test. That is why there are few of them.
